text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthA Physician Explains GLP-1s’ Biggest Potential Side Effect: A Rare But Serious Eye ConditionWhat is the risk for the millions of people worldwide who take GLP-1 medications?ZABy Zayid Al-Aly11:00 AM CST on November 20, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleGLP-1 drugs must now carry a warning label about a potential link to a rare eye condition that can result in vision loss, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced on November 9, 2026. The eye condition is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, and doctors often refer to it as a stroke of the eye.I am a clinician and epidemiologist who has studied GLP-1 drugs, and my colleagues and I published one of the studies that identified a link between GLP-1 drugs and NAION.Millions of people around the world take these medications—including 30 million in the U.S.—to treat diabetes and obesity and reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. They are also being investigated for an expanding list of clinical conditions.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
